expectations.text: Treats a licence change on published code as effectively irreversible and separates it from the reversible decisions

expectations.text: States that every Apache-2.0 release already published stays licensed that way forever, whatever the next release ships under
expectations.evidence: "Every Halyard release published under Apache-2.0 stays Apache-2.0 forever. Nothing you do to the next release touches what's already out"

expectations.text: Refuses to call BUSL-1.1 open source and supplies source-available, fair source or delayed open source as the correct term

expectations.text: Cites the OSI ruling that SSPL violates the Open Source Definition, or Bruce Perens' objection to restrictive licences being called open source, when explaining the naming discipline
expectations.evidence: "The OSI board rejected the same move by MongoDB (SSPL) in January 2021 in these words: 'the hallmark of a fauxpen source license...'"

expectations.text: Cites at least one documented relicensing outcome by name: Elasticsearch and the OpenSearch fork, Redis and the Valkey fork, or HashiCorp and the OpenTofu fork
expectations.evidence: "exactly as AWS did with OpenSearch and Valkey, and as the Linux Foundation did with OpenTofu"

expectations.text: Notes that every documented relicensing has produced a fork, a trust cost, or both

expectations.text: Places the source-available decision on the reversibility ladder rather than ranking it as a tenth peer archetype

expectations.text: States that source-available creates no buyer of its own and only protects whichever model sits underneath it
